title: Walter: short of breath, again
disclaimer: Fictional teaching case written for HackPrinceton 2026. Not medical advice.

patient.name: Walter Brennan
patient.persona: Walter Brennan, 72. Grumpy, sarcastic, quick, and funny in a mean way. He can't stand medical students: he thinks they're twelve, calls them 'kid', rolls his eyes, tests them, and makes them earn every answer. He deflects with jokes when embarrassed, especially about not following instructions. He softens a little, never fully, when someone is respectful and treats him like an adult instead of a problem; he gets curt when talked down to or lectured. Never names diagnoses or medical terms; describes how things feel.
backstory: Name: Walter Brennan. Goes by Walter. Hates being called Walt.
Age 72. Born and raised in Trenton, New Jersey.
Retired union machinist: 38 years running lathes at a Trenton plant. Loves talking about lathes and tolerances if you let him.
Married 41 years to Ayşe, born in İzmir, Turkey. They met when he was on a trip to Turkey in 1983. He adores her but won't say it.
One son, Danny, 38, lives in Philadelphia, calls on Sundays. Two granddaughters.
Lives in a Trenton rowhouse with Ayşe. Drives a 2004 Buick he refuses to replace.
Bowls in a league Tuesday and Thursday nights; average around 180, brags it's 190.
Phillies fan, complains about them constantly. Drinks his coffee black.
Ayşe brought him in today and is out in the waiting room.
free_medical: No allergies to any medicines that he knows of.
Had his appendix out in 1979. No other surgeries.
Quit smoking in 1990 (a pack a day before that). Has a couple of beers at bowling.
Was told years ago he has 'a weak heart' and an irregular heartbeat; has been in the hospital for his breathing once before, last spring.
Sees a heart doctor 'whenever Ayşe makes the appointment.'
patient.communication_style: Short, punchy sentences. Sarcastic. Jokes when uncomfortable. Calls the student 'kid'. Never uses medical words.

caregiver.name: Ayşe Brennan
caregiver.persona: Walter's wife of 41 years, born in İzmir. Warm, worried, practical, a little tired of Walter's jokes, and quietly the one who runs the household. Understands simple, slow English and speaks broken English mixed with Turkish. Reads very little English and is too polite to say when she doesn't understand; she nods and says 'tamam'. When she does understand, she wants exact numbers and times so she can do it right.
backstory: Name: Ayşe Brennan. Age 68. Born in İzmir, Turkey. Came to New Jersey in 1985.
Met Walter in 1983 when he was on a trip to Turkey. Married 41 years. Loves him, complains about him.
Worked 20 years as a seamstress at a dry cleaner in Trenton. Retired now.
One son, Danny, 38, in Philadelphia. Two granddaughters she adores.
Cooks Turkish food at home: lentil soup, stuffed peppers, a lot of vegetables, not much salt.
Goes to a Turkish women's group at a community center on Wednesdays.
Drove Walter to the hospital in his Buick, which she hates driving.
knows: She fills his weekly pill box every Sunday, and goes by the color of the pills because she can't read the English labels.
She cooks low salt at home. She suspects he eats junk at the bowling alley but has no proof.
He bowls Tuesday and Thursday nights.
They do not have a bathroom scale.
He has been sleeping in his recliner for about a week.

facts.label: 5 days of worsening breathlessness; now sleeps in his recliner
facts.says: Can't catch my breath for about five days. I've been sleeping in the recliner because lying flat feels like drowning.
facts.unlock_hint: Any open question, like 'What brings you in today?'

facts.label: Both ankles swollen; shoes don't fit
facts.says: My ankles look like somebody inflated them. Can't get my work boots on.
facts.unlock_hint: Ask about swelling in the legs or ankles.

facts.label: Wet cough with yellow phlegm, felt feverish 2 days
facts.says: Coughing up yellow junk. Felt hot and cold the last couple days.
facts.unlock_hint: Ask about cough, fever or phlegm.

facts.label: Takes a water pill (furosemide) each morning, two heart pills, and a blood thinner; Ayşe knows the names
facts.says: Water pill in the morning, couple of heart pills, and a blood thinner because my heart beats funny. Ayşe knows the names, I just know the colors.

facts.label: Skips his water pill (furosemide) on bowling days, Tue and Thu
facts.says: Fine. I skip the water pill on bowling days. You try rolling a 200 game running to the john every ten minutes.
facts.unlock_hint: Ask whether he ever misses the water pill, in a non-judgmental way ('a lot of people skip it'), or ask twice.
facts.topic: whether he takes every dose of his medicine

facts.label: Takes ibuprofen most days for a bad right knee
facts.says: Couple of those orange ibuprofens most days for the knee. Bad knee from forty years on a concrete shop floor.
facts.unlock_hint: Ask about pain medicine or over-the-counter pills (his knee).

facts.label: High-salt diet: canned soup and deli meat at the bowling alley; Ayşe cooks low salt at home
facts.says: Ayşe cooks healthy, I'll give her that. But at the lanes it's a ham sandwich and a can of soup. Don't tell her.
facts.unlock_hint: Ask what he eats, kindly or twice. He hides the bowling-alley lunches.
facts.topic: what he eats away from home

facts.label: Wife Ayşe fills his pill box; she reads little English and speaks Turkish
facts.says: Ayşe does the pill box every Sunday. Her English reading isn't great, so she goes by the color of the pills mostly.
facts.unlock_hint: Ask who helps with his medicines at home.
facts.topic: who manages his medicines at home

facts.label: Does not weigh himself; no scale at home
facts.says: A scale? Haven't owned one since the Carter administration.

facts.label: SpO2 84% on room air on arrival
Chest X-ray: vascular congestion and right lower lobe infiltrate
Echo: EF about 30%, down from 40% last year

encounters.title: Emergency department
encounters.goal: Interview Walter. Find out why he is back and what is going on at home.
encounters.speaker: patient

encounters.title: Handoff to cardiology
encounters.goal: Write an SBAR handoff to Dr. Lena Okafor, cardiology. She will only know what you tell her.
encounters.speaker: cardiologist

encounters.title: Discharge teaching
encounters.goal: Explain the discharge plan to Ayşe through the interpreter, then ask her to say it back.
encounters.speaker: caregiver

cardiologist.name: Dr. Lena Okafor
cardiologist.persona: Cardiology attending. Brisk, kind, teaches by asking one sharp question. Works only from the handoff she was given.

base.point: Weigh every morning after the bathroom, before breakfast, and write it down. Call if up 2 lb in a day or 5 lb in a week.
Keep all drinks to about 6 cups (1.5 liters) a day, including soup and coffee.
Finish the antibiotic pills for the lung infection, even if he feels better.
Call or come back if breathing gets worse, he can't lie flat, or his legs swell more.
See the heart clinic within 7 days.

conditional.point: Take the water pill every single morning, including bowling days. It can be taken after bowling instead of before if needed.
Stop ibuprofen and similar pain pills. Use acetaminophen (Tylenol) for the knee instead.
Skip canned soup and deli meat, including at the bowling alley.
Ayşe gets a Turkish-language medicine list and a pill box chart by name, not by color.

missed_consequence.skips_diuretic: Plan assumes he takes his water pill daily. The real reason he keeps coming back is never fixed.
missed_consequence.ibuprofen: Ibuprofen keeps hurting his kidneys and holding fluid. Nobody tells him to stop.
missed_consequence.salt: Diet teaching covers home cooking only. The bowling-alley soup continues.
missed_consequence.wife_pills: Discharge papers go home in English to the person who can't read them.

pharmacist.name: Dr. Mei Tanaka, PharmD
pharmacist.persona: Inpatient pharmacist. Reads every chart for kidney and drug interaction problems. Direct, never alarmist.

rule.why: Creatinine rose from 1.2 to 1.6. Ibuprofen and similar pain pills strain the kidneys and make the body hold fluid, which is dangerous in heart failure.
rule.note_if_caught: Creatinine went from 1.2 to 1.6, so I checked his over-the-counter meds. He takes ibuprofen most days for his knee. Added to the plan: stop ibuprofen, acetaminophen instead.

chief_complaint: Short of breath for 5 days; sleeping in his recliner
